title: File Handling
summary: Read and write text, CSV and JSON files.

exercises.title: Write and Read
exercises.prompt: Write `Hello file` to `notes.txt`, then read it back and print it.
hints: Use mode "w" then open again to read.
exercises.solution:
with open("notes.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Hello file")
with open("notes.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())

exercises.title: Three Lines
exercises.prompt: Write the lines `1`, `2`, `3` (one per line) to `nums.txt`, then read the whole file and print it.
exercises.solution:
with open("nums.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("1\n2\n3\n")
with open("nums.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())

exercises.title: Append Mode
exercises.prompt: Write `A` plus a newline to `log.txt`, append `B` plus a newline, then print the file contents.
exercises.solution:
with open("log.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("A\n")
with open("log.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("B\n")
with open("log.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())

exercises.title: Count Lines
exercises.prompt: Write three lines to `a.txt`, then use `readlines()` to print how many lines it has.
exercises.solution:
with open("a.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("x\ny\nz\n")
with open("a.txt") as f:
    print(len(f.readlines()))

exercises.title: Shout Each Line
exercises.prompt: Write the lines `red`, `green`, `blue` to `c.txt`. Read it line by line and print each in upper case.
hints: Loop over the file and strip each line.
exercises.solution:
with open("c.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("red\ngreen\nblue\n")
with open("c.txt") as f:
    for line in f:
        print(line.strip().upper())

exercises.title: Content Length
exercises.prompt: Write `Python` to `p.txt` using `with`, read it back, and print the length of the text.
exercises.solution:
with open("p.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Python")
with open("p.txt") as f:
    print(len(f.read()))

exercises.title: CSV Round Trip
exercises.prompt: Write the rows `["a", "b"]` and `["1", "2"]` with `csv.writer`, read them back with `csv.reader`, and print the list of rows.
exercises.solution:
import csv
with open("t.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["a", "b"])
    w.writerow(["1", "2"])
with open("t.csv", newline="") as f:
    print(list(csv.reader(f)))

exercises.title: JSON Round Trip
exercises.prompt: Save `{"name": "Asha", "age": 15}` to `s.json` with `json.dump`, load it back, and print the name.
exercises.solution:
import json
with open("s.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"name": "Asha", "age": 15}, f)
with open("s.json") as f:
    data = json.load(f)
print(data["name"])

exercises.title: Sum a File
exercises.prompt: Write `10`, `20`, `30` (one per line) to `n.txt`, read them back as integers, and print the sum.
exercises.solution:
with open("n.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("10\n20\n30\n")
with open("n.txt") as f:
    print(sum(int(line) for line in f))

exercises.title: Does It Exist?
exercises.prompt: Print `os.path.exists("missing.txt")`, then create that file (write `hi`) and print the check again.
exercises.solution:
import os
print(os.path.exists("missing.txt"))
with open("missing.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("hi")
print(os.path.exists("missing.txt"))
